title: The First Frost
note: Everything has a thin white edge.
light: Keep the lights cool and leave the paper bare where the frost catches.
shadow: for the cold blue shadows
highlight: for the frost on every rim and blade

title: Golden Hour
note: The sun sits low and everything it touches turns the colour of toffee.
light: Light just one side of each thing and pull its shadow out long behind it.
shadow: for the long shadows stretching away from the sun
highlight: for the sunlit side of each thing

title: A Rainy Sunday Afternoon
note: The rain has settled in for the day and the sky is one even grey.
light: Keep the values close together and save the white of the paper for the wet shine on things.
shadow: for the dim corners and the rain-dark patches
highlight: for the beads of rain on everything

title: The Blue Hour
phrases: a sky like ink stirred into milk
windows lighting up one by one
note: The sun has gone but the sky is still bright, and everything under it turns blue.
light: Wash everything in one cool blue first, then add any lamp or lit window as a warm spot on top.
shadow: for the deep blue of everything turned away from the sky
highlight: for the last brightness left in the sky

title: By Lamplight
phrases: the corners left to the dark
note: A single lamp makes a pool of light and everything outside it goes dim.
light: Decide where the lamp is, keep the brightest values right beside it and darken steadily as you move away.
shadow: for the dim edges beyond the lamp
highlight: for the surfaces turned towards the lamp

title: The Morning After Snow
when: on the morning after the snow
note: Fresh snow lies smooth over everything and the sky is scrubbed clear.
light: Leave the snow as untouched paper and shape it only with pale blue shadows in the dips.
shadow: for the sharp blue shadows in the snow
highlight: for the snow light bouncing up from below

title: A Storm Brewing
note: The clouds stack up dark and purple, and the light underneath turns strange and yellow.
light: Make the sky the darkest thing on the page and keep the ground lit, which feels backwards and looks right.
shadow: for the storm clouds and the deepest darks
highlight: for the odd, bright light under the clouds

title: Midsummer Night
when: on a midsummer night that never quite gets dark
phrases: a line of light in the north
note: Even at midnight a pale band of light lingers along the bottom of the sky.
light: Use a deep blue rather than black for the darks, and let the sky lighten towards one edge.
shadow: for the deep blue that stands in for black
highlight: for the pale band of sky that never goes out

title: A Misty Dawn
when: as the sun comes up through the mist
note: The sun is a flat, pale disc and anything far away dissolves into white.
light: Leave a round of bare paper for the sun and make each thing paler the further back it sits.
shadow: for the nearest shapes, the only ones with real darks
highlight: for the white sun and the mist around it

title: A Blustery Day
note: Clouds race across the sky and the sunshine keeps switching on and off.
light: Keep your strokes quick and slanted in one direction so the whole picture leans with the wind.
shadow: for the patches darkened by passing cloud
highlight: for the sudden bursts of sun

title: The First Warm Day
when: on the first warm day of spring
note: The air is mild, the light is clean and every bud looks about to pop.
light: Keep the colours light and clear, with yellowy greens and plenty of white paper showing.
shadow: for the short shadows of a high spring sun
highlight: for the new light on every upturned surface

title: After the Shower
phrases: a drop on every leaf tip
note: Everything is dripping and shining, and the sun is already back out.
light: Keep the colours rich and saturated, and leave a pinprick of paper on every drop and wet edge.
shadow: for the dark, rain-soaked patches
highlight: for the sparkle on every wet surface

title: Under a Full Moon
note: The moon is bright enough to throw real shadows, and all the colour has drained to silver and blue.
light: Work the darkest values first and leave the moonlit tops of things almost bare.
shadow: for the inky night shadows
highlight: for the moonlight on the tops of things

title: The Heatwave
note: The sun is high and white, the shadows shrink into tight pools and the air shimmers.
light: Bleach the sunlit areas almost to white and keep the shadows small, short and very dark.
shadow: for the small, deep shadows right underneath things
highlight: for the bleached, sun-struck tops of things

title: A Drizzly Tuesday
phrases: a sky that can't be bothered
note: A fine drizzle hangs in the air and the light stays flat all day.
light: Knock every colour back with a light layer of grey and keep the contrast low.
shadow: for the flat, damp greys
highlight: for the dull sheen on damp surfaces

title: The Dawn Chorus
phrases: the alarm not due for hours
note: Every bird for miles is singing and the sky is turning from grey to peach.
light: Run the sky from pale peach at the bottom to cool grey at the top, and keep everything below it dark.
shadow: for the dark shapes still waiting for the sun
highlight: for the peach light low in the sky

title: Teatime
note: The afternoon is winding down and the light comes in low and sideways.
light: Keep the lights creamy rather than white and the shadows a gentle brown, like an old photograph.
shadow: for the tea-coloured shadows
highlight: for the creamy late-afternoon light

title: The Harvest Moon
phrases: a moon the colour of apricots
note: An enormous orange moon hangs just above the horizon, much bigger than it has any right to be.
light: Make the moon the warmest, brightest thing in the picture and let every other colour cool down around it.
shadow: for the dusky blue of the evening
highlight: for the apricot moon and the light it spills

title: Bonfire Night
note: Smoke drifts low, the sky pops with colour and everything is lit orange from one side.
light: Plan the sparks first and leave them as bare paper, then work the night sky dark around them.
shadow: for the smoky night sky
highlight: for the bonfire light and the sparks

title: The Shortest Day
when: on the shortest day of the year
note: The sun hardly clears the treetops before it starts to sink again.
light: Keep the values low overall and save one band of pale, cold light for the sky near the horizon.
shadow: for the early dark creeping in
highlight: for the thin, cold light low in the sky

title: The Night Before Snow
when: on the night before the first snow
note: The clouds hang low and pinkish, and the air is so still you can almost hear it.
light: Make the sky paler than you would expect for night, a dull pinkish grey, with the ground darker beneath it.
shadow: for the still, heavy dark
highlight: for the strange pale sky before the snow

title: The First Morning of the Holidays
when: on the first morning of the holidays
note: The sun is already high by the time anyone gets up, and nothing needs doing.
light: Go light and loose, with lots of open paper and only a few firm darks.
shadow: for the few lazy shadows
highlight: for the high, unhurried morning light

title: While the Kettle Boils
note: Steam curls up from the spout and clouds the nearest window.
light: Blur a few edges with your palest colour, as if a little steam has drifted across the picture.
shadow: for the quiet indoor shadows
highlight: for the steam and the light on the window

title: By Firelight
note: The fire throws a flickering orange light and the shadows jump about on the walls.
light: Make the side facing the fire orange and bright, and let the far side drop straight into a deep, warm brown.
shadow: for the deep darks away from the fire
highlight: for the flickering orange on the side nearest the flames

title: Just After Breakfast
note: The morning light is clear and the day has only just got going.
light: Use clean, unmuddied colour and let the brightest patches of sun stay as plain paper.
shadow: for the neat morning shadows
highlight: for the clear early light

title: A Fog That Won't Lift
when: on a day when the fog won't lift
note: Fog sits over everything all day, and anything more than a few steps away simply disappears.
light: Draw the nearest things clearly, then make each thing behind them greyer and blurrier until it vanishes into the paper.
shadow: for the few darks close to you
highlight: for the white fog filling the distance

title: Blossom Time
note: The trees are thick with pink and white flowers, and petals drift past on the breeze.
light: Keep the pinks clean and pale, and use a cool green for the shadows so the blossom stays fresh.
shadow: for the cool, leafy shade
highlight: for the pale pink and white of the blossom

title: The Longest Evening
when: on the longest evening of the year
phrases: midges in the last of the sun
note: The sun takes forever to set and the sky stays warm and bright long after supper.
light: Run the sky from rose at the bottom to pale blue at the top, and keep the shadows a warm lilac.
shadow: for the lilac shadows of a late summer evening
highlight: for the rosy light that hangs on and on

title: A Crisp, Clear Morning
note: The sky is a hard, clear blue and every edge looks freshly sharpened.
light: Use a sharp point and firm edges, and keep the shadows a definite, cold blue.
shadow: for the clean blue shadows
highlight: for the bright, cold sunshine

title: Apple-Picking Weather
note: The days are mild and hazy, and the sun has a mellow, end-of-season warmth.
light: Lay a pale yellow haze over everything, then let the reds and russets carry the picture.
shadow: for the russet-brown shadows
highlight: for the sun on every rounded surface

title: An April Shower
note: Rain sweeps through in a hurry while the sun keeps shining somewhere behind it.
light: Draw the rain as a few light, slanting strokes of your palest blue and keep the sunlit parts bright.
shadow: for the slate-grey shower clouds
highlight: for the silver light through the rain

title: The Swallows Return
when: on the day the swallows come back
note: The sky is high and blue and full of quick, darting birds again.
light: Keep the sky big and pale, and let the strongest light sit on the tops of things.
shadow: for the quick, cool shadows of spring
highlight: for the high, clear April light

title: The Hour Before Sunrise
note: The sky is just beginning to pale, but the ground is still deep in night.
light: Work in dark blues and greys, and lighten only the sky along one edge, very slightly.
shadow: for the night that hasn't quite left
highlight: for the faint first paling of the sky

title: Starlight
when: under a sky full of stars
phrases: the Milky Way like spilt sugar
stars right down to the hedges
note: There is no moon, the sky is crowded with stars and everything below is a dark silhouette.
light: Press the stars into the paper first with an empty ballpoint pen, then layer the dark sky over them so they stay white.
shadow: for the night sky and the silhouettes
highlight: for the stars and the faint edges they catch

title: A Lazy Summer Afternoon
phrases: a book face down on the grass
note: The air hums with insects and nothing at all is in a hurry.
light: Keep the sunlight warm and a little blurry, and let the shade gather in pools of cool green or blue.
shadow: for the cool pools of shade
highlight: for the drowsy afternoon sunlight

title: Low Winter Sun
phrases: dust lit up in the air
note: The sun stays low all day and throws long, slanting light under everything.
light: Light everything from very low on one side and stretch the shadows right across the page.
shadow: for the very long, cold shadows
highlight: for the dazzle where the sun hits

title: Conker Season
when: on the first day of conker season
note: The air smells of damp leaves and the low sun warms everything to a glossy chestnut brown.
light: Burnish the brightest lights hard so they gleam like a new conker, and keep the shadows a rich brown.
shadow: for the deep chestnut browns
highlight: for the glossy shine on anything round and smooth

title: A Snow Day
note: Fat, slow flakes keep coming down and everything is hushed and white.
light: Keep the values pale and close, and save your darkest marks for the few things the snow hasn't covered.
shadow: for the few dark things the snow hasn't covered
highlight: for the snow, flake by flake

title: The Power Cut
when: by candlelight in a power cut
note: One candle flame lights a small circle and the rest of the room disappears into dark.
light: Pick one bright point for the flame, let the light fade quickly around it and keep everything else very dark.
shadow: for the big dark beyond the candle
highlight: for the trembling circle of candlelight

title: Wet Leaves Underfoot
note: Wet leaves lie stuck to everything and the light is damp, brown and quiet.
light: Use muddy browns and dull oranges, then add a few sharp wet highlights so the leaves glisten.
shadow: for the earthy, sodden darks
highlight: for the shine on wet leaves
